reasons.text: Certificates claim more than the declared monthly capacity in 100% of months
73% of feedstock comes from collectors invoicing far beyond their declared capacity
Category III share of certificates is 67%, +65% versus what its process route can produce
62% of purchase invoices have suspiciously round tonnages (typical plant: about 2%)
Electricity bought is only 0.48x the minimum needed for the tonnes claimed (143 kWh/t against at least 300)
35% of high-value consignments have no e-way bill

inspection_checklist: Check installed machinery and shift records against the declared capacity; request production registers for the flagged months.
Visit the named collectors: confirm premises, vehicles and storage; check their registration dates and sales to other buyers.
Cross-check the certificate generation dates and category mix against the plant's process route and stock registers.
Physically verify a sample of purchase invoices with the sellers (weighbridge slips, e-way bills, vehicle logs).
Obtain the DISCOM consumption statement and meter readings for the flagged months; compare connected machinery (kW) against the claimed tonnage.
